stem: After an adverse event that harmed a client, the care team prepares for disclosure to the client and family. Which approach best reflects AHRQ CANDOR guidance?

options.A: Delay disclosure until litigation is resolved and all uncertainty has disappeared.
options.B: Explain the known facts honestly without speculation, respond with empathy, and outline next steps and follow-up.
options.C: Avoid expressions of concern or apology because they always establish legal liability.
options.D: Have one unprepared clinician conduct the disclosure without team preparation or organizational support.

rationale: AHRQ CANDOR guidance recommends timely, honest and compassionate disclosure. The team should prepare for the conversation, explain known facts without speculation, listen and respond empathically, apologize appropriately, and describe next steps and follow-up. Therefore B is correct.
educational_objective: Apply AHRQ CANDOR principles for transparent, compassionate communication after a harmful adverse event.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_version_date: Page last reviewed August 2022; current AHRQ CANDOR toolkit rechecked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Disclosure Checklist — Part II: Get Ready; Listen and Empathize Throughout; Explain the Facts; Apologize; Close the Discussion
source_claim_supported: CANDOR disclosure includes team preparation, honest explanation of known facts without speculation, empathic listening, appropriate apology, discussion of next steps and follow-up, and documentation.
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — communication, client rights, incident response and quality/safety
correction_summary: Removed conversational padding and the unsupported universal legal claim about expressions of empathy. Reframed the item around exact AHRQ CANDOR disclosure behaviors and team preparation. Difficulty set to medium.
audit_findings: AHRQ CANDOR directly supports B. A conflicts with timely disclosure, C makes an unsupported universal legal assertion, and D conflicts with recommended preparation/support. Independent second pass confirmed B is uniquely correct.
